title: PagSAMDC4a ‐Mediated Polyamine Synthesis Regulate Vessel Differentiation Under Drought Stress Conditions in Poplar

sections.abstract: Frequent and prolonged drought stress is a primary factor limiting the growth and development of perennial woody plants. Xylem vessel cells are crucial for water transport in woody plants; however, the molecular mechanisms governing the changes in their morphogenesis in response to water deprivation remain unclear. Here, we report that the alterations in polyamine (PA) levels under drought stress, mediated by the key enzyme PagSAMDC4a in PA synthesis, influence vessel morphogenesis through the modulation of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) concentration in poplar 84 K ( Populus alba × Populus glandulosa ). PagSAMDC4a expression was predominantly observed in the phloem and cambium zones of stems and was upregulated under drought conditions. Overexpression of PagSAMDC4a ( PagSAMDC4a ‐OE) resulted in increased PA content, leading to reduced vessel size and density in stem xylem. Conversely, PagSAMDC4a mutant lines exhibited the opposite phenotype, resembling 84 K plants treated with the PA synthesis inhibitor methylglyoxal‐bis (guanylhydrazone). In addition, PagSAMDC4a ‐OE exhibited improved drought tolerance compared to nontransgenic 84 K plants and PagSAMDC4a mutant lines. Interestingly, the H 2 O 2 level was significantly decreased in PagSAMDC4a ‐OE plants but markedly increased in PagSAMDC4a mutants relative to 84 K plants, suggesting that changes in vessel size may result from altered H 2 O 2 levels. Supporting this hypothesis, H 2 O 2 application rescued the small vessel phenotype in PagSAMDC4a ‐OE, whereas the scavenger potassium iodide reduced the size of xylem vessels in PagSAMDC4a mutants. Collectively, these findings provide evidence for the role of PAs in enhancing drought tolerance through the regulation of vessel differentiation.
sections.introduction:
Water scarcity is a critical factor that constrains the survival and productivity of perennial woody plants (Anderegg et al. 2013 ; Senf et al. 2020 ; Hammond et al. 2022 ). In response to water deficiency, trees have developed intricate physiological and morphological mechanisms to alleviate cell damage caused by drought stress. These mechanisms encompass modifications in the root system to enhance hydraulic uptake, adjustments in the size and number of xylem vessels within the stem to preserve water conductivity, and alterations in stomatal status to minimise transpiration from leaves (Dash et al. 2017 ; Levionnois et al. 2021 ; He et al. 2018 ). Given the necessity for perennial woody plants to transport water across considerable distances to support their growth (Couvreur et al. 2018 ), secondary vascular systems are crucial in mitigating the detrimental impacts of drought on these species.

The secondary vascular system in woody plants is generated through the sustained activity of the vascular cambium, a layer of meristematic cells that continually produce daughter cells on both abaxially and adaxially through periclinal division. The adaxial cells undergo expansion, cell wall thickening, programmed cell death and eventually differentiation into xylem cells (Courtois‐Moreau et al. 2009 ; Du and Groover 2010 ; Spicer and Groover 2010 ; Fischer et al. 2019 ). Xylem vessels, which are derived from elongated cells, serve to provide a conduit for water transport. The size and morphology of these vessels are critical for both the efficiency of water transport and the capacity to recover from embolisms induced by drought stress (Zwieniecki and Holbrook 2000 ). The differentiation of xylem cells is regulated by a complex network of transcription factors and phytohormones (Ye and Zhong 2015 ; Fischer et al. 2019 ; Du et al. 2011 ; Robischon et al. 2011 ; Zhong et al. 2006 , 2008 ; Zhou et al. 2014 ; Hunziker and Greb 2024 ).

Plant hormones are crucial for regulating the development of vascular tissues under both normal and stress conditions. Indole‐3‐acetic acid (IAA) is notably concentrated in the cambium zone, where it significantly influences cambium activity and xylem differentiation (Gouwentak 1941 ; Sundberg et al. 2000 ; Little et al. 2002 ). Cytokinin modulates cambium activity and coordinates the development of secondary phloem and cambium (Fu et al. 2021 ). Overexpression of AtIPT7 , which increases cytokinin levels, has been shown to enhance cambium activity and biomass production in poplar (Nieminen et al. 2008 ; Immanen et al. 2016 ). Conversely, overexpression of PtoMYB142 in poplar reduces gibberellin (GA) levels, leading to a decrease in the lumen area of xylem vessels, thereby preventing cavitation and improving water transport (Song et al. 2024 ). Jasmonic acid (JA) promotes secondary cell wall (SCW) formation by upregulating genes involved in lignin biosynthesis and enhances drought tolerance through the regulation of stomatal closure and reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging (Sehr et al. 2010 ; Liu et al. 2021 ; Singh et al. 2021 ; Rao et al. 2023 ; Zhou et al. 2019 ). Peptide hormones such as PtCLE24/28/47 positively regulate cambial activity, resulting in increased secondary xylem formation (Han et al. 2016 ; Kucukoglu et al. 2020 ).

Polyamines (PAs), considered as hormones, are multifunctional aliphatic amines found in various plant species (Tabor and Tabor 1984 ). The four primary biogenic polyamines in plants—putrescine (Put), spermidine (Spd), spermine (Spm) and thermospermine (T‐spm)—are synthesised from amino acids through the enzymatic activities of arginine decarboxylase (ADC) or ornithine decarboxylase (Gao et al. 2021 ; Handa and Mattoo 2010 ; Liu et al. 2015 ; Takahashi 2020 ). Put serves as the principal precursor in the biosynthetic pathway, leading to the formation of spermidine via spermidine synthases, spermine via spermine synthases and thermospermine via thermospermine synthases (ACL5) (Walters 2003 ; Tiburcio et al. 2014 ). S‐adenosylmethionine donates the aminopropyl group necessary for the synthesis of spermidine and spermine, a process catalysed by S‐adenosylmethionine decarboxylase (SAMDC). Consequently, SAMDC is recognised as a critical rate‐limiting enzyme in the polyamine biosynthesis pathway (Hu et al. 2005 ). Compared with the polyamine biosynthetic pathway, the PA degradation pathway remains relatively underexplored. Polyamine metabolism in plants is catalysed by polyamine oxidases that also produce signalling molecules such as H 2 O 2 and nitric oxide (NO) (Diao et al. 2017 ; Moschou et al. 2008 ). H 2 O 2 and NO serve as critical secondary messengers in PA‐mediated signalling pathways during various developmental processes, senescence and stress responses in plants (Gupta et al. 2016 ; Liu et al. 2019 ; Peng et al. 2016 ). Polyamines and H 2 O 2 jointly regulate rice mesocotyl elongation via the interaction between ethylene and jasmonic acid (JA) signalling pathways (Lv et al. 2021 ), while polyamines can also activate plant defence mechanisms through the ROS‐dependent salicylic acid pathway (Liu et al. 2020 ). Furthermore, T‐Spm and NO may interact to modulate leaf vascular development and seed size (Mai et al. 2024 ). Under stress conditions, H 2 O 2 and NO influence gene expression by regulating cytosolic potassium homeostasis and calcium signalling, thereby triggering a cytoprotective stress response to mitigate oxidative damage (Pottosin et al. 2012 ). Further research into the interconnections between PAs, H 2 O 2 and NO during plant growth and development is essential.

PAs play a crucial role in regulating various aspects of biological processes, such as chromatin structure modifications, maintenance of cell membrane integrity, oxidative stress responses and intercellular communication (Lenis et al. 2017 ; Borromeo et al. 2023 ; Van Den Broeck et al. 1994 ; Du et al. 2022 ; Gill and Tuteja 2010 ). Notably, the Arabidopsis double mutants of ADC1 and ADC2 result in plant lethality (Sánchez‐Rangel et al. 2016 ), while ACL5 is predominantly expressed in differentiating xylem vessels and is upregulated by exogenous auxin treatment (Muñiz et al. 2008 ; Hanzawa 2000 ). Additionally, the Arabidopsis samdc mutant shows severely impaired internode elongation and excessive xylem vessel formation (Ge et al. 2006 ). These findings suggest that PAs are likely involved in xylem development. On the other hand, accumulating evidence indicates that PAs can enhance plant tolerance to abiotic stress (Alcázar et al. 2020 ). Under salt stress, PAs can inhibit cation channels, maintain ion homeostasis and thus improve plant salt tolerance (Su et al. 2019 ; Alcázar et al. 2010 ; Saha et al. 2022 ). PAs can also mitigate lipid peroxidation by downregulating the NAD(P)H‐oxidase activity under drought stress (Gill and Tuteja 2010 ). Moreover, the accumulation of endogenous PAs typically serves an antioxidant function by directly eliminating ROS or by activating the ROS‐scavenging enzyme system under adverse conditions (Jahan et al. 2022 ; Hassan et al. 2018 ). Interestingly, the application of exogenous PAs can significantly increase the activity of peroxidase and catalase, leading to a reduction in ROS synthesis during dehydration in citrus (Shi et al. 2010 ). These findings collectively demonstrate that polyamines serve as central regulators in plant stress responses through osmoprotection, antioxidant defence, signal transduction and synergistic interactions with other hormones. Additionally, they also indicate the involvement of polyamines in vascular tissue development. However, the mechanisms by which the stress response triggers the expression of PA‐related genes, as well as the processes linking PA accumulation, increased ROS levels and xylem differentiation, remain largely unexplored.

In this study, we have demonstrated that the accumulation of PAs in response to water stress results in enhanced drought resistance by reducing the vessel size and number in hybrid poplar 84 K ( Populus alba × P. glandulosa ). Consistent with this finding, the overexpression of poplar SAMDC ( PagSAMDC4a ), which leads to elevated PA levels, was associated with a decrease in vessel size and number, thereby improving drought tolerance. Conversely, the knockout of PagSAMDC4a leading to the reduced PA levels produced the opposite effect. Additionally, our research indicates that H 2 O 2 levels play a mediating role in the modification of xylem vessel size. This study not only provides new insights into the molecular mechanisms regulating the plant's response to water deficit via the modification of xylem vessel differentiation, but also paves the way for alteration of wood properties by precisely manipulating PAs through molecular techniques in poplar.
sections.results:
We selected 2‐month‐old 84 K poplars and treated them with drought stress to determine the change in PAs content following stress exposure. After 3 days of treatment, the levels of Put and Spd content were significantly increased, while Spm showed no significant change. However, after 7 days, all PA levels were significantly higher compared with the untreated controls (Figure 1a,b ). To investigate the effect of PAs on drought tolerance in poplars, we treated poplars with PAs or SAMDC inhibitor methylglyoxal‐bis (guanylhydrazone) (MGBG), and simultaneously stopped watering. Control and MGBG‐treated plants displayed severe leaf wilting, whereas PAs‐treated poplars remained largely unaffected under drought conditions (Figure 1c,d ). We measured the leaf relative water content (LRWC) and found that PAs‐treated poplars had higher LRWC compared with control and MGBG‐treated plants (Figure 1e ). In addition, the PAs‐treated plants exhibited significantly lower values of electrolyte leakage (EL) and malondialdehyde (MDA) content under drought stress, although all plants showed similar values under well‐watered conditions (Figures 1f and S1a ). These results suggest that the application of PAs improves the drought resistance of poplars. Interestingly, the H 2 O 2 content was elevated in MGBG‐treated plants even in the absence of drought stress, as compared to the control group, and this increase was more pronounced under stress conditions (Figure S1b ). This finding suggests a close relationship between PA levels and H 2 O 2 .

To further investigate the changes in vascular tissues, we examined the stem cross‐sections of PA‐treated plants using microscopy. The results indicated that MGBG‐treated plants exhibited an increased size and number of xylem vessels, whereas Put, Spd and Spm treatments showed no significant differences compared to untreated plants under normal watering conditions (Figure 2a–c ). To evaluate the differentiation of xylem vessels under prolonged drought stress, poplars were cultivated in soil with a moisture content of 20%. After 21 days of treatment, hindered growth and leaf abscission were observed compared to plants under normal irrigation conditions (Figure S2a ). Examination of stem cross‐sections revealed a significant reduction in the size, as represented by lumen area, of newly differentiated xylem vessels under drought stress (Figure S2b ,c). These findings indicate that PAs may contribute to poplar's tolerance to water deficiency by modulating xylem vessel differentiation.

(b, c) Statistical analyses of the vessel lumen area (b) and vessel number (c). Data are presented as means ± SD. **p < 0.01; ns, no significance, t ‐test.

To investigate whether altered PA levels can influence xylem cell differentiation, we aimed to modulate the PA levels by overexpression or knockout of the rate‐limiting enzyme gene SAMDC . A total of six SAMDC genes were identified in the Populus genome (Figure S3a ,b) and their expression patterns in different tissues of 84 K poplar were determined using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT‐qPCR). Notably, PagSAMDC4a and PagSAMDC4b exhibited elevated expression levels in phloem and cambium tissues (Figure 3a and S4a). Furthermore, according to data from the AspWood database (Sundell et al. 2017 ), PtSAMDC4a and PtSAMDC4b were specifically expressed in the cambium and xylem expansion zone, contrasting with the expression patterns of other PtSAMDC genes (Figure S4b ). These results suggest that these two genes may play a role in the PAs synthesis in wood‐forming tissues. Additionally, we examined the expression of PagSAMDC4a under drought conditions, and observed a significant induction of PagSAMDC4a expression in stems, reaching up to 5‐fold at 5 h under mannitol treatment (Figure 3b ), and a notably higher expression at 3 days in stems and 7 days in leaves under water‐deficient conditions (Figure 3c ). In contrast, PagSAMDC4b did not exhibit any response to drought (Figure S4c ). Consequently, PagSAMDC4a was found to be the only member specifically expressed in wood‐forming tissues and responsive to drought stress. To further examine tissue‐specific expression of PagSAMDC4a , we isolated a 1996 bp promoter region to drive the expression of the β‐glucuronidase ( GUS ) gene, which was subsequently transformed into poplar. Histochemical staining of the entire plant revealed a strong blue signal in young stems and leaves, with more specific GUS staining observed in the vascular tissues of the stem through cross‐sectioning and in the roots (Figure 3d ). Additionally, GUS activity in the stems of these transgenic plants was induced by drought (Figure 3e,f ). These findings suggest that PagSAMDC4a may play a crucial role in the synthesis of PAs in vascular tissues under water‐deficit conditions in poplar.

To further elucidate the role of SAMDC4a in the biosynthesis of PAs in 84 K poplar, we generated PagSAMDC4a overexpression lines (OE‐L15 and OE‐L17) (Figure S5a ) and knockout PagSAMDC4a lines using the CRISPR/Cas9‐based genome editing system. We obtained two homozygous PagSAMDC4a mutant lines, designated as KO‐4 and KO‐8 (Figure S5b ). These transgenic lines exhibited no significant differences in plant height or basal diameter (Figure S5c,d ), but demonstrated significant alterations in the Spd and Spm contents of their stems compared to 84 K (Figure S5e ). Notably, Spd content increased by 46.5% and 45.7% in the PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines L15 and L17, while it was reduced by 34.7% and 30.4% in the KO‐4 and KO‐8, respectively. We also checked the expression levels of PAs synthesis‐related genes, including SPDS and SPMS in PagSAMDC4a ‐OE plants, and found they were significantly upregulated. In contrast, no significant differences in their expression were observed in the knockout lines (Figure S6 ). These findings suggest that PagSAMDC4a indeed plays a key role in PAs synthesis in poplar stem.

We further prepared the cross‐sections of the 11th internode and observed the vascular tissues with a microscope after staining with toluidine blue O (TBO). The PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines exhibited a narrowed xylem width and reduced xylem occupancy in the stem, while the PagSAMDC4a mutants showed no significant differences compared with the 84 K control (Figure 4a–c ). Notably, the PagSAMDC4a mutant displayed an increased number and size of vessels, in contrast to the PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines, which showed a decrease in both vessel number and size compared with the 84 K control (Figure 4d–f ). To characterise the properties of xylem cells, we macerated the vessels and fibres from the 8th internode and observed them under a microscope (Figure S7a ). The PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines had smaller vessels, with 8.8% (L15) and 24.9% (L17) reduction in width, while the PagSAMDC4a mutants exhibited larger vessels with 10% (KO‐4) and 22.8% (KO‐8) increase compared with the 84 K control (Figure S7b ). In addition, PagSAMDC4a mutant lines had wider fibre cells with a 17% (KO‐4) and 21% (KO‐8) increase in size compared with the 84 K control, respectively (Figure S7c ). Furthermore, MGBG treatment of PagSAMDC4a ‐OE plants resulted in pronounced changes in the wood anatomy, including reduced xylem width and increased lumen area of vessels (Figure S8 ). This phenotype resembles that of the PagSAMDC4a mutants, suggesting that the abundance and activity of PagSAMDC4a influence PAs, which in turn modulates the differentiation of xylem vessels in poplar.

Different letters denote statistically significant difference by Tukey's test, with p < 0.05.

To further assess the role of PagSAMDC4a in response to water‐deficient conditions in poplar, 2‐month‐old 84 K, PagSAMDC4a ‐OE, and PagSAMDC4a mutant plants were subjected to drought treatment (Figure S9a ). After a 10‐day drought treatment, the PagSAMDC4a ‐OE line maintained a healthy growth state, whereas the 84 K plants exhibited drought symptoms, including drooping leaves, and the PagSAMDC4a mutants showed even more severe symptoms, such as wilted leaves and crooked apical buds (Figure S9b ). We further measured soil relative water content (SRWC), LRWC, EL, H 2 O 2 levels and MDA content. Before and after short‐term drought treatment, no significant differences in SRWC were observed between the 84 K and the PagSAMDC4a transgenic lines (Figure S9c ). Under water‐sufficient conditions, the LRWC, EL and MDA values of 84 K, PagSAMDC4a ‐OE and PagSAMDC4a mutants were similar; however, under drought stress conditions, these values were significantly different. In contrast to the PagSAMDC4a mutants and 84 K control plants, PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines exhibited higher LRWC and lower levels of EL and MDA content in leaves under drought stress, indicating a high cell viability maintained after stress (Figures 5c,d and S9e ). Furthermore, despite the elevation of H 2 O 2 levels across all genotypes under drought stress, this increase was notably lower in the PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines compared with the significantly higher levels observed in the PagSAMDC4a mutants (Figure S9d ). Following a 10‐day short‐term drought treatment, we investigated the differentiation of xylem vessel cells across different internodes in PagSAMDC4a transgenic plants. In all lines, the newly differentiated xylem vessels were significantly smaller compared with those under normal conditions (Figure S10a–c ). A long‐term drought stress experiment was conducted on these poplar lines by maintaining the SRWC at 15% for 1 month. The PagSAMDC4a mutants and 84 K leaves displayed leaf wilting and drying, with the PagSAMDC4a mutants exhibiting more severe symptoms, whereas the PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines continued to grow normally, apart from the shedding of some lower leaves (Figure 5a,b ). To explore the impact of PagSAMDC4a misexpression on the development of vascular tissues under drought stress, we examined the morphology of the newly differentiated xylem in the 5th internode postdrought treatment using microscopy (Figure 5e,f ). The PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines showed a marked reduction in xylem width under both normal and drought stress conditions (Figure 5g ). While all lines exhibited increased xylem vessel density and reduced lumen area under drought conditions, the PagSAMDC4a ‐OE and PagSAMDC4a mutants represented the two extremes (Figure 5h,i ). These results indicate that PagSAMDC4a plays a crucial role in regulating xylem differentiation in response to water deficiency.

(g–i) Statistical analysis of xylem width (g), vessel lumen area (h), and vessel number (i). Different letters denote statistically significant difference by Tukey's test, with p < 0.05.

H 2 O 2 , one of the ROS, was found to be significantly altered in PagSAMDC4a transgenic plants under both normal and stress conditions (Figure S9d ). To investigate whether PagSAMDC4a could modulate ROS levels, 1‐month‐old 84 K and transgenic plants were stained with nitro blue tetrazolium (NBT) and 3, 3′‐diaminobenzidine (DAB) to detect O 2 ⸱− and H 2 O 2 , respectively. The intensity of stains on cross‐sections revealed that the O 2 ⸱− and H 2 O 2 levels were lower in PagSAMDC4a ‐OE while higher in the PagSAMDC4a mutants, compared with those in 84 K (Figure 6a–d ). This finding was corroborated by the quantification of O 2 ⸱− and H 2 O 2 in the stems of these plants (Figure 6e,f ). The contents of PAs in plants have been shown to influence the respiration burst oxidase homologues (RBOH)‐mediated oxidation pathway in an antagonistic manner (Papadakis and Roubelakis‐Angelakis 2005 ). Consequently, the enzyme activities of RBOH and superoxide dismutase (SOD) in the stems were measured, revealing that both RBOH and SOD activities were significantly elevated in PagSAMDC4a mutants, compared to PagSAMDC4a ‐OE and 84 K poplars (Figure 6g,h ). Therefore, we further examined whether the altered PA content resulting from the overexpression or knockout of PagSAMDC4a would impact the gene expression of RBOHs and SODs . Based on the phylogenetic and AspWood data analysis of RBOH genes, we selected 5 RBOH genes that were highly expressed in cambium and further validated them using RT‐qPCR (Figure S11a,b ). The result revealed that these five RBOH genes were upregulated in the stems of PagSAMDC4a mutant, and three of these genes displayed opposite expression patterns in PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines, compared with the 84 K control (Figure S11e ). Additionally, all 10 SOD genes (Figure S11c , d) were analysed in transgenic lines and their expressions were consistently higher in the stems of PagSAMDC4a mutant compared with those of 84 K control (Figure S11f ). We performed RT‐PCR to check the expression of PagSOD and PagRBOH genes in 84 K plants under PAs and MGBG treatment. The levels of PagRBOH02 , PagRBOH06 and PagRBOH10 at 6 or 12 h (Figure S12a ), and PagCSD2a , PagCSD2b , PagCSD3a, PagCSD3b and PagMSD1/2b at 12 or 36 h post MGBG treatment were significantly increased (Figure S12b ). However, no significant differences were detected in the expression patterns of these PagSOD and PagRBOH genes under PAs treatment. These results may explain the changes in vessel morphology in MGBG‐treated stems but not in PA‐treated stems. Collectively, these findings suggest that the altered expression of PagSAMDC4a may influence the endogenous ROS levels in poplar by modulating the expression of RBOH and SOD genes and the activity of their encoded enzymes.

To further investigate whether the changes in the number and size of xylem vessels in transgenic plants were due to the alterations in H 2 O 2 levels caused by the overexpression and knockout of PagSAMDC4a , we applied H 2 O 2 and its scavenger potassium iodide (KI) to PagSAMDC4a transgenic plants (Figure 7a,d ). The result demonstrated that H 2 O 2 significantly increased xylem width and size in PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines with low endogenous H 2 O 2 levels (Figure 7b,c ). Conversely, KI treatment led to a significant decrease in vessel size and vessel density in PagSAMDC4a mutants with high endogenous H 2 O 2 levels (Figure 7e,f ). Based on these results, we propose the hypothesis that PagSAMDC4a functions in xylem vessel differentiation through the regulation of H 2 O 2 levels.

sections.discussion:
Drought, as a critical environmental factor, significantly impacts the growth and development of trees. To acclimate to arid conditions, woody plants have evolved a series of adaptive morphological modifications, such as an increase in the number and a reduction in the size of xylem vessels to mitigate the risk of vessel embolism and enhance the water transport efficiency of roots and stems (Arend and Fromm 2007 ; Fichot et al. 2009 ). Furthermore, drought stress typically elicits a range of physiological responses in plants, including alterations in polyamine levels, the accumulation of osmotic compounds and the synthesis of ROS‐related proteins (Alcázar et al. 2020 ; Bhatnagar‐Mathur et al. 2008 ). However, the molecular mechanism governing how these multifaceted responses coordinate to influence vascular tissue differentiation remains largely unexplored. This study elucidates that the modulation of PAs content by SAMDC4a activity is pivotal in regulating the density and size of secondary xylem vessels in poplar under drought conditions, a process mediated by H 2 O 2 levels.

Previous studies have demonstrated that PAs can enhance plant stress resistance via multiple mechanisms, such as enhancing osmoregulatory substances, activating the antioxidant system to reduce ROS (Zhang et al. 2014 ; Li et al. 2015 ; Yang et al. 2022 ), thus mitigating the adverse effects of dehydration stress (Hassan et al. 2018 ; Shi et al. 2010 ). This study comprehensively investigated the role of PAs in drought tolerance through both exogenous application and endogenous alteration of PA levels through genetic modifications. We firstly observed an increased PAs level in poplar plants exposed to drought stress, which remained consistently high under prolonged stress conditions (Figure 1b ). Subsequently, we confirmed the involvement of PAs in stress tolerance by applying PAs and MGBG, an inhibitor of SAMDC in PA synthesis, demonstrating increased and decreased drought tolerance in the treated poplars, respectively (Figure 1c,d ). The inhibition of SAMDC resulted in severe damage, suggesting its critical role in PAs‐mediated drought tolerance. Therefore, we selected SAMDC4a , showing high expression in vascular tissues and responsive to drought stress, to generate PagSAMDC4a overexpression and knockout poplar lines with significantly increased and decreased PAs content, respectively (Figures 3 and S5e ). Consistently, the transgenic lines with overexpressing PagSAMDC4a exhibited enhanced drought resistance, whereas the PagSAMDC4a knockout lines displayed increased sensitivity to drought stress (Figure S9b ). Collectively, both the exogenous and endogenous alterations in PA levels affect the drought tolerance of poplars.

It has been proposed that PAs play a role in xylem development (Kakehi et al. 2008 ; Mai et al. 2024 ). For instance, T‐spm synthetase Arabidopsis mutant atacl5 had decreased endogenous T‐spm levels and demonstrated delayed xylem development (Takano et al. 2012 ). In this study, we revealed that xylem vessel development was significantly influenced in plants treated with the SAMDC inhibitor MGBG, which resulted in enlarged vessels (Figure 2 ). Furthermore, transgenic lines overexpressing PagSAMDC4a , leading to elevated PA levels, displayed decreased vessel size, whereas lines with reduced PA levels due to the knockout of PagSAMDC4a exhibited larger vessel sizes (Figure 4 ). Additionally, overexpression of PagSAMDC4a enhanced drought resistance, while the knockout of PagSAMDC4a decreased drought tolerance (Figure 5a ). It has also been observed that woody plants increase the number of xylem vessels while reducing their size to adapt to drought conditions (Arend and Fromm 2007 ; Fichot et al. 2009 ). These findings strongly support the hypothesis that PAs enhance drought tolerance by modulating vessel size. Indeed, the PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines with reduced vessel diameters exhibited higher LRWC, presumably by mitigating drought‐induced cavitation, thereby improving water transport to plant organs (Choat et al. 2012 ). Therefore, this study provides new insights into the adaptive mechanisms of woody plants to drought stress through alterations in PA levels. Specifically, the elevated levels of PAs via the overexpression of PagSAMDC4a significantly reduce the number and diameter of vessels, particularly under drought conditions, whereas the reduced levels of PAs through the knockout of PagSAMDC4a promote the formation of more and larger vessels even in the presence of drought stress (Figure 5f ). These results reinforce the role of PAs in enhancing drought tolerance by regulating vessel differentiation.

Many studies have demonstrated that reactive oxygen species (ROS) play a crucial role in regulating plant meristem cell division and differentiation. Specifically, the balance between O 2 ⸱− and H 2 O 2 determines whether cells will proliferate or differentiate (Tsukagoshi et al. 2010 ; Yamada et al. 2020 ). Recent findings indicate that LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES DOMAIN 11 ( LBD11 ) regulates the proliferation and radial growth of Arabidopsis cambium cells by activating the transcription of genes involved in ROS metabolism, thereby increasing ROS levels (Dang et al. 2023 ). Moreover, elevated O 2 ⸱− levels during tension wood induction trigger downstream IAA signalling pathways, which not only promote cambium cell proliferation but also facilitate advanced PCD (Huang et al. 2024 ). Given the reduced number of xylem vessels in tension wood compared to normal wood, high levels of O 2 ⸱− may have an inhibitory effect on vessel differentiation. On the other hand, H 2 O 2 , as a key signalling molecule, plays a pivotal role in modulating the expression of numerous genes related to growth and development (Bordenave et al. 2019 ; Sagor et al. 2013 ). Specifically, H 2 O 2 is involved in the modulation of leaf cell expansion and final organ size in maize ( Zea mays ) (Lu et al. 2014 ). The elevated PAs content can act as ROS scavengers, thereby playing an essential role in redox homeostasis (Das and Misra 2004 ; Ha et al. 1998 ; Liu et al. 2020 ). However, the precise mechanism through which PAs mediate vessel development via H 2 O 2 in woody plants remains unclear. In this study, both ROS staining and quantitative measurement of the ROS contents revealed a decrease in O 2 ⸱− and H 2 O 2 levels in PagSAMDC4a ‐OE plants, whereas these levels were elevated in PagSAMDC4a mutant related to 84 K plants (Figure 6a–f ). Additionally, the expression of RBOH and SOD enzyme genes was upregulated in PagSAMDC4a mutant, accompanied by an increase in enzyme activity, while the opposite trend was observed in PagSAMDC4a ‐OE plants (Figures 6g,h and S11 ). These findings suggest that the increase in H 2 O 2 levels may predominantly result from a reduction in antioxidant enzyme activity due to the elevated PAs content, which in turn alters vessel morphology by influencing H 2 O 2 levels. Furthermore, exogenous H 2 O 2 treatment effectively restored secondary xylem development in PagSAMDC4a ‐OE plants, comparable to the 84 K control, including xylem width and vessel size (Figure 7a–c ). On the other hand, the size and density of xylem vessels in PagSAMDC4a mutant were markedly reduced following KI treatment (Figure 7d–f ). Therefore, this study provides substantial evidence supporting the notion that PagSAMDC4a regulates vessel development by modulating H 2 O 2 concentration.

Based on our data, we propose a working model illustrated in Figure 8 . Under normal conditions, PagSAMDC4a is expressed at moderate levels, maintaining appropriate concentrations of PAs and H 2 O 2 , which results in the formation of vessels of normal size in poplar, supporting optimal growth of the plants. The knockout of PagSAMDC4a leads to reduced endogenous PA levels, which subsequently increases the activities of RBOH and SOD enzymes, resulting in higher H 2 O 2 levels. Consequently, this induces an increase in vessel size and enhances the plants' sensitivity to drought stress. Conversely, drought‐induced high expression of PagSAMDC4a in poplars, as observed in PagSAMDC4a ‐OE lines, increases endogenous PA levels, further reducing H 2 O 2 levels, leading to a xylem morphology with small vessels that is resistant to water deficiency.

Hypothetical model proposes for the mechanism of PagSAMDC4a mediated PAs levels involved in vessels differentiation in normal and in response to drought stress. Knockout of PagSAMDC4a leads to a reduction in PAs content, subsequently enhancing the activity of RBOH and SOD enzymes. This results in increased H 2 O 2 accumulation, which contributes to the formation of larger xylem vessels and consequently diminishes the drought tolerance of the knockout lines. Under normal conditions, moderate expression of PagSAMDC4a regulates vessel differentiation to an appropriate size, maintaining normal plant growth. Conversely, under drought stress, PagSAMDC4a expression is upregulated, promoting PAs synthesis while suppressing RBOH and SOD enzyme activities, thereby reducing H 2 O 2 levels. This process further exacerbates the reduction in xylem vessel cells, ultimately enhancing plant drought resistance. The red arrow indicates the increase (↑) or decrease (↓) of the levels, the black arrow (→) represents positive regulation or promotion, the arrow with a cross (⊣) denotes negative regulation or inhibition. The thickness of the arrows represents the magnitude of the regulatory effect.

In conclusion, our study reveals that the fine‐tuning of PA levels, modulated by PagSAMDC4a expression in response to drought stress, plays a critical role in regulating vessel differentiation, thereby enhancing resilience against water deficiency in poplar. Additionally, these findings offer a promising effective strategy for simultaneously enhancing drought tolerance and wood properties in poplar through genetic manipulation.
